items.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 29, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: When John Coltrane played out, at least I know where he is.

ctx.x: Speaking of that. Are you a fan of the Coltrane type music and that era where people played on and on and on?

When John Coltrane played out, at least I know where he is. Some people play out and I don’t know where they are. You know. I’m not a fan of out. A little bit out, but I want to hear the song, or I want to hear a reference to a song. I want to know where the band is, where everybody is. For those who haven’t heard it, when Coltrane said to Miles, or Miles said to Coltrane, “listen man, you’ve got to stop playing those 45 minute solos. items.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, November 11, 2017 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I don’t think John Coltrane sat down in his living room one day and said — you know — I mean I think he was reaching but I don’t think he said, I think tonight I’m going to do this just to sound different.

ctx.x: Why don’t you like the word “artistic”?

It gets thrown around too easy. “Oh I’m an artist.” Really? You paint? That’s what I think. An artist is somebody who creates a sculpture or a painting or something. I mean there are some guys that are musical artists. Let me go back to I hear Charlie Parker was an artist. No he wasn’t. Maybe he was a genius I don’t know. Maybe he was an artist. Maybe he was. But to me he was an innovator. And I don’t think he set out to be one, it happens. I don’t think John Coltrane sat down in his living room one day and said…

different baby, we can’t use you, sorry.” I mean those guys weren’t even recognized at first because they were too different. “You’re too different man, can’t you just fall in?” “Well if I fall in then I’m going to be just like everybody else.”
